1. PURPOSE

This report is the follow-up to the initial incident report (RRT-A/2026/114) concerning the contamination of the drinking water supply in Jagnath Plot, Ward 7, on the night of 20–21 August 2026. It documents the response actions taken after the initial containment, the results of confirmatory testing, coordination with medical and water departments, and the final outcome and lessons learned.

2. BACKGROUND SUMMARY (FROM INITIAL REPORT)

On 20 Aug 2026, at approximately 17:40 hours, the District Emergency Operations Centre (DEOC) received a report from the Ward 7 Health Post of multiple cases of acute gastroenteritis among residents of Jagnath Plot. Initial investigation suggested a possible link to the municipal water supply. The District Collector was informed and directed the activation of Rapid Response Team Alpha. The team assembled at 19:10 hours and deployed to the site. Preliminary field testing of water samples at 23:30 hours on 20 Aug indicated the presence of coliform bacteria. A cracked sewage pipe was discovered approximately 1.2 metres from the drinking water line during excavation at 06:00 hours on 21 Aug. Repair work was initiated and completed by 07:30 hours. The water line was chlorinated, and post-chlorination samples were collected at 08:45 hours on 21 Aug and sent to the RMC laboratory for confirmatory testing. Refer to Report RRT-A/2026/114 for the full initial timeline.

3. FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS AND CHRONOLOGY (CONTINUATION FROM 21 AUG 2026, 08:45 HOURS)

The following table details the sequence of events following the collection of post-chlorination samples.

4. MEDICAL OUTCOME SUMMARY

A total of 46 persons were treated at the medical camp for symptoms consistent with gastroenteritis (diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal cramps). The majority of cases were mild and resolved with oral rehydration salts and symptomatic treatment. Five patients required intravenous fluids for moderate dehydration. All patients were discharged by the time the camp closed. No severe complications, hospital admissions, or deaths were reported. The age range of affected persons was 2 years to 71 years. The final case count is consistent with the initial estimate of 38 symptomatic persons at the time of the first survey, with the additional 8 cases presenting later at the medical camp on the morning of 21 August.

5. COORDINATION WITH WATER WORKS DEPARTMENT

The RMC Water Works Department played a critical role in the response. Key coordination points:

documents.title: Incident Report: Water Contamination Scare
documents.content:
INCIDENT REPORT – RAPID RESPONSE TEAM ALPHA
Water Contamination Scare – Jagnath Plot, Ward 7, Rajkot
Follow-up and Resolution Report
Report No: RRT-A/2026/114-F2
Reference: RRT-A/2026/114 (Initial Report, dated 21 Aug 2026)
Date of Report: 22 Aug 2026
Submitted by: Team Leader, RRT Alpha
Submitted to: District Collector, Rajkot; Director, District Emergency Operations Centre; Municipal Commissioner, Rajkot Municipal Corporation (RMC)

---

1. PURPOSE

This report is the follow-up to the initial incident report (RRT-A/2026/114) concerning the contamination of the drinking water supply in Jagnath Plot, Ward 7, on the night of 20–21 August 2026. It documents the response actions taken after the initial containment, the results of confirmatory testing, coordination with medical and water departments, and the final outcome and lessons learned.

2. BACKGROUND SUMMARY (FROM INITIAL REPORT)

On 20 Aug 2026, at approximately 17:40 hours, the District Emergency Operations Centre (DEOC) received a report from the Ward 7 Health Post of multiple cases of acute gastroenteritis among residents of Jagnath Plot. Initial investigation suggested a possible link to the municipal water supply. The District Collector was informed and directed the activation of Rapid Response Team Alpha. The team assembled at 19:10 hours and deployed to the site. Preliminary field testing of water samples at 23:30 hours on 20 Aug indicated the presence of coliform bacteria. A cracked sewage pipe was discovered approximately 1.2 metres from the drinking water line during excavation at 06:00 hours on 21 Aug. Repair work was initiated and completed by 07:30 hours. The water line was chlorinated, and post-chlorination samples were collected at 08:45 hours on 21 Aug and sent to the RMC laboratory for confirmatory testing. Refer to Report RRT-A/2026/114 for the full initial timeline.

3. FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS AND CHRONOLOGY (CONTINUATION FROM 21 AUG 2026, 08:45 HOURS)

The following table details the sequence of events following the collection of post-chlorination samples.

4. MEDICAL OUTCOME SUMMARY

A total of 46 persons were treated at the medical camp for symptoms consistent with gastroenteritis (diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal cramps). The majority of cases were mild and resolved with oral rehydration salts and symptomatic treatment. Five patients required intravenous fluids for moderate dehydration. All patients were discharged by the time the camp closed. No severe complications, hospital admissions, or deaths were reported. The age range of affected persons was 2 years to 71 years. The final case count is consistent with the initial estimate of 38 symptomatic persons at the time of the first survey, with the additional 8 cases presenting later at the medical camp on the morning of 21 August.

5. COORDINATION WITH WATER WORKS DEPARTMENT

The RMC Water Works Department played a critical role in the response. Key coordination points:

- The WWD engineer was on site within two hours of the initial alert.
